people-who-paid-irish-citizenship-firms-.author: Madison Ciére
people-who-paid-irish-citizenship-firms-.core: Posted in last 7 days People Who Paid Irish Citizenship Firms - Misled by Ancestry Claims Hi, bit of a weird one… I’m currently working on an investigative feature about companies that market Irish citizenship services to people with Irish ancestry, including those whose family connections may be too distant to qualify under Irish citizenship law. You probably know the sort of companies I’m talking about. The ones whose advertising makes an Irish passport sound remarkably straightforward, even when the reality can be rather different. I’m particularly interested in cases where people have paid thousands for assistance, only to spend years waiting for citizenship they may never have been eligible for in the first place. I want to look at how these services are advertised, what customers are actually promised, and what happens when things don’t work out. I’d really like to hear from anyone with experience of this. Have you used one of these companies? Do you know someone who has? Perhaps you’ve paid a considerable amount of money and still feel misled, or you’re still waiting for answers years later. I’d especially appreciate hearing from people who feel they’ve been taken advantage of, though I understand discussing this publicly might be uncomfortable. I’m also interested in hearing from anyone with strong opinions on the subject, personal experiences, or information they think deserves a closer look. If you think these companies provide a genuinely valuable service, I’d be interested in hearing that perspective, too. Please feel free to send me a private message if you’d rather not comment publicly. Anonymity in the published article is guaranteed for anyone who requests it. I appreciate that this could be a sensitive or embarrassing experience to discuss, and nobody should feel uncomfortable coming forward. Any information, experiences or leads would be hugely appreciated. I suspect there’s quite a story here, and I’d like to hear from the people who’ve actually dealt with these companies.

west-end-and-harbor-bay-alameda-resident.core: Posted in last 7 days West End & Harbor Bay Alameda Residents - Halloween Yard Displays Bear’s-Eye View of Alameda for October 11, 2026 Welcome to Halloween 2026MOUF FOR MAYOR – Campaign Update Earlier this week, I received a link from Ready Jensen for a zoom meeting to discuss a possible endorsement of his human companion Tracy Jensen who is also running for mayor. During our meeting, he let me know that he was also a rescue, that Tracy has been a big supporter of the animal shelter, and is keenly aware of the failed condition of the building. I will be meeting with the Jensen team later today to see what they are proposing for upgrading the shelter. Stay tuned for an update shortly. This week, Alameda residents kicked their Halloween decorating efforts into high gear with major installations popping up all around town. I am starting out with the smaller ones since they tend to get passed over for the larger more elaborate ones. However, one of my favorite installations is located in Santa Clara Avenue and was completed this week. This is a multimedia display that always delights. For those feline enthusiasts, the Kittens of the Catibbean is back and just as purr-fect as last year’s version. Aliens returned to this driveway on Encinal Avenue with another great invasion. You need to check this one out at night when the eerie green lights are on. You can imagine hearing “Mulder is that you? Mulder?” in the background. The perfect example of what can happen if you live on a diet of Coca-Cola is hanging out on a lawn over in Alameda Avenue. I guess things don’t always go better with Coke. I was happy to see two of my favorite witches fly back into town for this annual haunting event. There were plenty of dragons and dinosaurs inflatables around, and I expect more to show up in the coming weeks. Over on Harbor Bay, there was a nice dining scene complete with the family canine begging for food from the table. As the nights get shorter and the days get colder, I will be making my human companion get me out for all of my walks even though he hates it when it gets dark early, and he has to put on ski gloves to keep warm. If you see a guy dressed like he lives at the North Pole with a handsome German Shephard mix out front, that's us. Please honk. gen-z-adults-18-growing-up-with-disturbi.core: Posted in last 7 days Gen Z Adults 18+ - Growing Up With Disturbing Online Content Did you see disturbing things online as a kid? I'm a journalist looking to hear your experiences. Hi everyone! I'm a Gen Z journalist and editor-in-chief of Xpress Magazine at San Francisco State University, and I'm working on an investigative feature about what it was like growing up on the internet in the 2000s and 2010s. The idea actually came from a conversation with friends about the things we encountered online as kids — gore videos, shock sites like LiveLeak, Rotten.com and BestGore, pornography, Omegle, disturbing YouTube videos and other content we probably weren't old enough to understand. It got me wondering: Now that we're adults, what, if anything, did growing up with access to that kind of content leave behind? I've been interviewing psychologists and media researchers and looking into historical studies documenting children's exposure to disturbing online material. Now, I really want to hear from people who actually lived through it. I'm interested in hearing: What do you remember seeing online as a kid that you probably shouldn't have? How old were you, and how did you come across it? How did you react at the time? Looking back now, do you think those experiences affected you in any way — or not at all? I'm looking for Gen Z adults who would be willing to participate in a short interview for a magazine story. I'm interested in all perspectives, including people who don't feel their childhood internet experiences affected them. If you're interested, please comment or DM me! I'm happy to share more about the story and the publication before arranging an interview. You don't need to share graphic details publicly, and please don't post or send graphic or explicit material. Thank you! Xpress Magazine

directors-vps-and-clevel-execs-past-12-m.headline: Directors VPs & C-Level Execs - Past 12 Months Relocation Negotiation
directors-vps-and-clevel-execs-past-12-m.author: Sarah Johnston
directors-vps-and-clevel-execs-past-12-m.core: Posted in last 7 days Directors VPs & C-Level Execs - Past 12 Months Relocation Negotiation Have you negotiated a corporate relocation in the past 12 months? I'd love to hear what you learned. I'm working on an article about negotiating corporate relocation, and I'm looking to hear from Director-, VP-, and C-level professionals who have recently negotiated a relocation package. Relocation packages can involve much more than moving expenses. I'm interested in the details candidates may not think to ask about until they're in the middle of a move. I'd love to learn about your experience, including: The money: Was your package a lump sum, reimbursement, or company-managed relocation? Were you able to negotiate the amount? The fine print: Was there a repayment clause if you left the company within a certain period? Did you negotiate those terms? The timing: When did you first ask about relocation during the interview process? At what point did you understand exactly what was covered—and what wasn't? The family factor: Were you able to negotiate support for a spouse's career, school enrollment, temporary housing, or other family needs? The unexpected: What do you wish you'd known or negotiated before accepting the offer? I'm especially interested in the things you wouldn't necessarily find in a company's relocation policy. What worked? What surprised you? What would you do differently? I'd love to send you a few questions by email that you can answer on your own time. You can also contribute anonymously if you prefer. If you've been through this process recently and are willing to share your experience, please comment “RELOCATION” or send me a private message. I'd be grateful for your insights! I will be sharing what I learned in my newsletter (Career Briefs) And if you know someone who has recently negotiated a corporate relocation, please feel free to tag them.

Im trying to write a video essay on queerness in the American political right. I want to hear about some of your experiences with being qieer and either accepting or repressing it while on the right.
